latest.title: Entropy of Noncommutative Spaces
latest.summary: We give an overview of the second quantisation of spectral triples and compute the entropy of the noncommutative space described by it in terms of a spectral action. This reviews earlier work by Chamseddine, Connes and the second author, but presented here concisely, including the procedure of second quantisation using infinite-dimensional Clifford algebras. We exemplify the theory by considering noncommutative metric spaces consisting of $N$ points. The entropy of these discrete spaces is explicitly computed, and we study the resulting entropic force as well as the evolution of the spaces in time.

latest.title: NeuroMASS v4: Geometry-Aware Neural Population Dynamics via Learnable Hyperbolic Latent Representations and Biologically-Calibrated Diagonal State Space Models
latest.summary: The geometry of neural population activity is a fundamental challenge in computational neuroscience. We present NeuroMASS v4, a novel architecture that introduces learnable hyperbolic latent geometry to spike-train co-smoothing on the Neural Latents Benchmark (NLB'21). Endogenously cleaved microtubule-binding region tau 243 (eMTBR-tau243) has shown promise when measured by mass spectrometry; a scalable immunoassay could broaden research access and support clinical evaluation. latest.summary: Quantum effects in biological systems are increasingly investigated at molecular, cellular, and neural scales, yet evidence for quantum organization in a living brain does not by itself determine the ontological status of the conscious states realized by that brain. This article distinguishes seven claims often compressed under "quantum consciousness": quantum occurrence, causal relevance, constitutive relevance, phenomenal bridging, phenomenal individuation, quantum mental status, and quantum-formal adequacy. It argues that evidence for the first three-even if decisive-does not by itself establish quantum mental status. I call this cross-level inferential discontinuity the Ontological…

items.title: Supporting ethical engagement with AI in education: Evaluating the ethical coverage of the Scaffolded AI Literacy (SAIL) framework
items.summary: Ethical engagement with AI in education requires more than awareness of risks or compliance with institutional policy. Educators and learners need to recognise, evaluate, mitigate, and respond to ethical issues as AI tools become embedded in learning and teaching. This paper examines whether the Scaffolded AI Literacy (SAIL) framework provides a sufficiently comprehensive set of competencies for this purpose. Six cross-sector systematic reviews and mappings of AI ethics are analysed to provide a benchmark of recurring ethical issues identified in relation to AI. items.summary: Preregistration of a secondary analysis of the public Helsinki neonatal EEG dataset (79 newborns, seizures annotated second by second by three experts; Stevenson et al. 2019, doi:10.1038/sdata.2019.39; Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.4940267, CC BY 4.0). items.title: Experimental Approaches for Quantifying the Desolvation Step in Aqueous Reaction Equilibria
items.summary: Conspectus This Account focuses on recent studies aimed at detecting and quantifying changes in surface hydration, as needed to define the contribution of water in biothermodynamics. Solvation details are vital for the analysis of binding and conformational equilibria; knowledge of desolvation energies may improve the design of molecular structures and lead to therapeutics of higher specificity, in addition to elucidating the forces that drive all biomolecular interactions in a living cell. A central question for this field of research is the adequacy of the thermodynamic equation employed for describing reaction equilibria in water. We maintain that the classical equation represents an…

items.title: ScaleVLA: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models to 552 Billion Parameters
items.summary: Frontier Vision-Language Models (VLMs) such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in robot control, suggesting that broad pretraining provides knowledge valuable for physical action. Yet most Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies still rely on much smaller VLM backbones, leaving this potential largely untapped. We ask whether frontier-scale representations can provide a stronger foundation for robot learning. We introduce ScaleVLA, which connects a 552B DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash backbone to a trainable action DiT, and systematically compare VLMs from 2B to 552B under a shared training setup. We evaluate three fundamental capabilities of robot foundation models. In sample…

items.title: Connectivity from activity in spiking neural networks
items.summary: We show that a wide range of recurrent neural network models obey a simple set of equations tying synaptic connectivity and single-cell response properties to neural correlations. Our modeling framework considers networks in a stationary, asynchronous state and contains a broad class of synaptic filters, spiking nonlinearities, and random-plus-structured connectivity. The resulting equations naturally decompose into contributions from monosynaptic, disynaptic, and higher order paths through the network. We leverage this decomposition to express the effective monosynaptic connection between two neurons in terms of experimentally measurable statistics of the activity, and in particular,…

items.title: When Do Histology Foundation Models Need Geometric Test-Time Augmentation?
items.summary: Test-time augmentation (TTA) aggregates model predictions across multiple transformed views of an input during inference. Because histology images lack a canonical orientation, $D_4$ TTA---pooling across the 8 rotations and reflections of a square---is a standard default in computational pathology. However, the rise of self-supervised histology foundation models (FMs) with inherent rotational invariance calls its continued utility into question. We benchmark 9 histology FMs and 6 general-purpose models across four patch-level and two whole-slide image (WSI) datasets. We find that $D_4$ TTA remains a reliable post hoc improvement, but benefits diminish from $+1.98$ percentage points (pp)…

items.title: Severe but Harmless: Stress-Testing Shift Severity for Frozen Time-Series Forecasters
items.summary: Zero-shot time-series foundation models (TSFMs) have become attractive alternatives to task-specific models because they handle diverse downstream tasks, including anomaly detection and forecasting, without per-series training. However, time-series data undergo distribution shifts, and the dissimilarity between two regimes is commonly scored with statistical measures such as Wasserstein-1, where a higher score is read as a more severe shift. In systematic experiments using three established severity measures on nine regime shifts from three standard traffic datasets, we show that these measures do not reliably predict degradation for instance-normalized TSFMs. The regimes rated most severe…

items.title: FM-Recon: Exploring Foundation Model Features for Accelerated Cardiac Cine MRI Reconstruction
items.summary: Foundation models have demonstrated strong feature extraction capabilities across various medical imaging tasks, yet their potential for MRI reconstruction remains largely unexplored, particularly within unrolled reconstruction networks and under artifact-corrupted inputs. In this work, we explore whether and how features from pretrained foundation models can benefit accelerated cardiac cine MRI reconstruction. To this end, we propose FM-Recon, a framework that refines and integrates extracted features from frozen image encoder of foundation models into an unrolled reconstruction network. Through extensive experiments on the CMRxRecon2023 dataset, we systematically evaluate foundation…

items.title: Open-fMIND: A Large-Scale Open-Access fMRI Corpus for Pretraining Brain Foundation Models
items.summary: Self-supervised pretraining has transformed language and vision, but its application to functional MRI (fMRI) is constrained by data access. The largest standardized fMRI resources are governed by data use agreements and dominated by a small number of acquisition protocols, while the thousands of openly licensed datasets on OpenNeuro are individually small, heterogeneously organized, and unprocessed. We present the first release of Open-fMIND, a uniformly preprocessed, openly accessible corpus of parcellated fMRI timeseries from 322 OpenNeuro studies, comprising 11,379 subjects and 45,731 functional runs. Each run is preprocessed with fMRIPrep and parcellated under 52 atlases spanning 14…

items.title: Scribble Once, Segment the Sequence: Bidirectional Temporal Consistency for Weakly Supervised Segmentation in Echocardiography Sequences
items.summary: Temporal medical image segmentation relies on pixel-wise annotations, which are prohibitively expensive for long image sequences. Existing weakly-supervised methods reduce the annotation burden per frame but still require repeated annotations across the sequence. Furthermore, sparse supervision can result in temporally unstable representations. Addressing both challenges requires a model that can leverage strong spatial priors from large-scale pretraining while minimizing reliance on dense annotations. Frozen 2D vision foundation models provide a promising basis for this by offering transferable spatial representations with low trainable parameters. However, their lack of explicit temporal…

items.title: Region-VAD: Video Anomaly Localization and Detection via Region Selection
items.summary: Anomalies are local events, yet weakly supervised video anomaly detection scores them globally. Most methods pool an entire frame into a single vector, rank frames by that vector, and derive a location afterwards as a saliency map of the score. Full-frame pooling mixes the anomaly with its background, so a detector can reach competitive benchmark scores from scene context without being able to show where in the scene the anomaly occurs. We introduce Region-VAD, which first selects a region and then detects the anomaly from that region alone. Region-VAD selects an explicit rectangle over the tokens of a frozen foundation model and scores anomalousness only from the tokens inside the box,…

items.title: Evaluation-Free Recursive Self-Improvement for Coding Agents
items.summary: Recent self-improving coding agents have achieved strong benchmark performance by iteratively modifying their own executable implementations. A common pattern uses downstream task-derived evidence to decide which candidates or lineages continue evolving, which we term evaluate-and-select. Obtaining this signal requires repeatedly executing evolved agents on downstream tasks, so broader exploration incurs increasing evaluation cost, while repeated optimization against a fixed evaluation distribution may encourage benchmark-specific adaptation. We ask: can coding agents self-improve without downstream task evaluation inside the evolution loop? We introduce Explore-then-Integrate (ELITE),…

items.title: Calpha: Toward Native Biomolecular Intelligence in a General-Purpose Language Model
items.summary: Biomolecular foundation models predict the structures of proteins and their complexes accurately, and large language models (LLMs) reason in natural language, but the two remain separate: the abilities of the former are not part of a general-purpose LLM, and the reasoning of the latter does not enter a structure prediction. Calpha aims at one general model that folds proteins and complexes, understands protein sequence and structure, and lets its language reasoning influence the structures it predicts. This report covers the first step, in which an LLM outputs single-chain protein structures. Qwen3.5-9B reads a sequence enriched with ESM2 residue features. It can respond in text or emit a…

items.title: Interpretable deep concepts of organoid morphology
items.summary: Image-based classification of organoid morphologies can indicate drug response, viability, or successful differentiation. In recent work, learned representations outperform handcrafted features as the basis for downstream classifiers. However, their black-box nature hides the morphological cues a classifier relies on. Based on the foundation models DINOv3 (general-purpose) and ViTAMIn-O (organoid-specific), we train sparse autoencoders (SAEs) to learn interpretable concepts related to distinct organoid morphologies. We annotate concepts with spatial labels (organoid, organoid wall, background) and compute their dataset specificity and task relevance across five tasks. The spatial labels of…

items.title: A Recursive Construction of Perfect Arrays of Every Shape $2^{a_1}\times\cdots\times2^{a_d}$ over the Unit Quaternions
items.summary: We extend the recursive construction of perfect and odd perfect sequences over the simple unit quaternions $\Qe=\{\pm1,\pm i,\pm j,\pm k\}$ of Blake to arrays of any dimension. The three operations of that construction act on one direction of an array at a time, and are valid whenever the array is periodic in the remaining directions. Starting from a perfect array $P$ of shape $M_2\times\cdots\times M_d$ they give perfect arrays of shape $2^a\times M_2\times\cdots\times M_d$ for every $a\ge0$, with explicit index functions and with the array orthogonality property for the divisor $2$ in the lifted direction; from $a=5$ on these arrays are, in general, Kronecker products of a sequence with…

items.title: VA-Assembly: View-Aligned Score Guidance for Training-Free 3D Part Assembly
items.summary: Image-to-3D foundation models have improved 3D reconstruction, but typically produce monolithic representations without explicit part-level structure. Part-aware generation and learning-based assembly methods often require part-level supervision, category-specific priors, or paired part-layout training data. We instead consider a practical but underexplored setting in which independently prepared or generated 3D parts have no predefined inter-part relationships, shared coordinate frames, or consistent scales, and must be assembled into a reference-consistent object from a single image. We present VA-Assembly, a training-free framework for 3D part assembly through part-level transformation…

items.title: A Seismic Foundation Model for Dense Feature Extraction
items.summary: Deep-learning-based seismic interpretation is constrained by scarce high-quality annotations, and most existing models are trained separately for individual tasks. We present SeisDFE, a 7B-parameter seismic foundation model for dense feature extraction, pretrained on 5.34 million 2D images derived from more than 500 seismic volumes. A three-stage pretraining strategy, combining discriminative self-supervised learning, Gram feature anchoring, and multi-resolution adaptation, improves feature discriminability while preserving spatial coherence. With its encoder frozen, SeisDFE supports seismic facies classification, salt detection, fault detection, and relative geologic time estimation. It…

items.title: Robotic Reward Models in the Foundation-Model Era
items.summary: Robotic reward models (RRMs) use foundation models to replace per-task reward engineering with reusable, task-conditioned evaluation. Yet under one name, their outputs answer different questions, from whether a task succeeded to which execution is better. This survey organizes 114 methods into five semantic families by the question their native outputs answer: Outcome, Absolute Progress, Relative, Temporal Value, and Hybrid. Within this taxonomy, we review how model design determines what an evaluator can judge, how raw experience becomes supervision, and how existing evaluation practice tests the result. The review exposes a gap: agreement with demonstration order and downstream policy…

items.title: A note on Padmanabhan's path-integral duality
items.summary: We develop a field-theoretic implementation of Padmanabhan's principle of invariance under the duality $\mathcal S \rightarrow {L_0^2}/{\mathcal S}$, where ${\mathcal S}$ is the proper length (the action integral along a particle's trajectory) and $L_0$ is a quantum of length. Starting from the particle propagator and its Schwinger proper-time representation, we derive the wave operator associated with the duality transformation in terms of a scalar field, rather than a point particle. The resulting theory is governed by a nonlocal operator involving modified Bessel functions. We analyse the infrared and ultraviolet regimes, demonstrate the recovery of standard Klein-Gordon theory at low…

items.title: Boson Stars with Ayón--Beato--García nonlinear electrodynamics
items.summary: In this paper, we study spherically symmetric boson star solutions in Einstein gravity minimally coupled to Ayón--Beato--García nonlinear electrodynamics and a massive complex scalar field. We find that these solutions exist only when the electric charge $q$ is below a critical value. Within this range, solutions with relatively small charges can exhibit a gravitational blueshift, and the radial mass function becomes negative in some regions while the ADM mass remains positive. For larger charges, frozen boson-star solutions emerge as the scalar-field frequency $ω$ approaches zero. items.title: Progressive Layer-wise Supervision: Deep-to-Shallow Supervision Annealing for Efficient and Robust Speech Deepfake Detection
items.summary: Speech foundation models pretrained via self-supervised learning provide powerful representations for deepfake detection, yet we find that standard fine-tuning exploits only the deepest transformer layers-leaving the majority of the network's capacity discriminatively inert. Layer-wise probing of XLS-R-128 reveals that the top two-thirds of the transformer stack contribute negligibly to anti-spoofing performance after standard fine-tuning, a phenomenon we term shallow-layer dormancy. We connect this observation to the representational redundancy of pretrained transformers: adjacent layers encode highly similar information, and fine-tuning without explicit intermediate supervision…

items.title: SCoRe: Support-Calibrated Role Fusion for Training-Free Cross-Domain Few-Shot Segmentation
items.summary: We present SCoRe (Support-Calibrated Role fusion), a framework to utilize two complementary vision foundation model-based (VFM) segmenters for training-free cross-domain few-shot segmentation (CD-FSS). Our approach is based on the observation that current VFMs for CD-FSS possess capabilities where one model locates the correct object, while another model computes the better contour. Our approach uses: 1. a method to identify a VFM segmenter to lead Few-Shot Segmentation (FSS) task for a given concept, 2. a novel deterministic boundary correction method using bands of near- and far-pixels at the lead segmenter's predicted boundary of an object, and 3. a region correction mechanism for the…

items.title: Harmonic branches of Einstein--ModMax--scalar field gravity: exact solutions and regularity II
items.summary: We integrate harmonic solution branches of Einstein--ModMax--Scalar field gravity, keeping the electromagnetic phase \(\tanΘ=\mathcal{G}/\mathcal{F}\) non-constant. For each family we first solve the field equations $(a(\s),b(\s),c(\s))$ and reconstruct the physical functions $f,ω,k,A_t,A_\varphi,φ$. In the same section we then select the Schwarzschild or Coulomb harmonic function, impose the regular horizon conditions, identify the ModMax solution, and state its Maxwell limit. Two theorems distinguish a constant electromagnetic phase from an exact static charge rescaling and show how twist prevents constant diagonal rescalings of the electromagnetic potentials at fixed metric and scalar.…

items.title: Lift, See, Act: Hierarchical Robot Policy Pretraining with 3D Foundation Models
items.summary: Robot policy pretraining based on human videos is crucial for improving the policy's generalization ability. One main challenge for this task is the lack of explicit action-relevant representations in such unlabeled data. Recent works tend to estimate 3D hand motion trajectories from videos using 3D foundation models (3D FMs). However, they keep solely the sparse trajectories as supervision, ignoring the rich, fine-grained information produced during the trajectory extraction process. To address this issue, we propose LSA, a hierarchical robot policy pretraining framework that includes three phases: Lift, See, and Act. Specifically, the Lift phase elevates 2D video observations into dense…

items.title: Tabular Foundation Models as Emulators for Forecasting Terrestrial Ecosystem Dynamics
items.summary: Process-based terrestrial biosphere models such as the Ecosystem Demography (ED) model underpin global carbon budgets, but their cost limits global, high-resolution and scenario-rich simulation. Deep emulators such as DeepED reduce that cost but require task-specific architectures and training. Tabular foundation models offer a different route: TabPFN predicts new rows by in-context learning, without being trained on the task. We compare TabPFN-3.5 with two DeepED baselines, $DeepED_{LSTM}$ and $DeepED_{Transformer}$, on CarbonGlobe's overall evaluation, which trains on a uniform 1/16 sample of sites and tests on the other 50,779, predicting the 40-year state of all seven ED outputs. items.title: AdaModalX: Synchronization-Free MFM Inference for Distributed Multimodal Mobile Sensing via Progressive Data Orchestration
items.summary: Multimodal foundation models (MFMs) support generalizable inference in distributed mobile sensing applications by integrating heterogeneous data streams. However, existing MFM inference pipelines typically require complete and synchronized multimodal inputs, whereas mobile sensing streams arrive asynchronously due to network variability and heterogeneous data volumes across modalities. Waiting for all modalities increases end-to-end latency, while inference with incomplete inputs can reduce accuracy. We argue that multimodal inference should depend on the utility of available information rather than modality completeness. Based on this principle, we propose AdaModalX, a progressive…

items.title: Taint Analysis via Heap-Aware Propagation
items.summary: Taint analysis for C depends on how precisely the analysis tracks tainted values as they flow through memory objects. Without field sensitivity, a tainted object field can spuriously taint an entire object, producing significant false alarms. In this paper, we present a field-sensitive taint analysis that combines Data Structure Analysis (DSA) for field-sensitive points-to information with a data-flow analysis for tracking explicit dependencies. We identify that existing DSA-style analyses lose precision on a common object pattern: a C struct object that mixes scalar fields with a flexible array member. items.title: TrainExplorer: Autonomous LLM Post-Training via Plan-and-Decouple Exploration
items.summary: LLM-based agents can automate model post-training, accelerating progress toward recursive self-improvement. Despite their promise, existing approaches remain under-explored and face two main challenges: (1) strategy lock-in that limits exploration beyond the initial strategy; and (2) coupled execution that obscures the effects of individual modifications. To address these challanges, we propose TrainExplorer, a multi-agent framework for autonomous post-training, that incorporates strategy planning and execution decoupling, to achieve broaden strategy exploration. First, strategy planning draws on scientific literature to construct a candidate search space of training strategies. Then,…

items.title: FiuMD: Heterogeneous Batching for Coarse-Grained Molecular Dynamics with Neural Network Potentials
items.summary: FiuMD is a GPU molecular dynamics engine that advances many independent biomolecular simulations as a single batch, even when the systems differ in size, topology, force-field parameters, periodic box, timestep, or thermostat parameters. All systems are concatenated into global tensors, so the classical interaction terms and a shared TorchMD-Net neural network potential are evaluated for the whole batch at once, while each system keeps its own integration and thermostat. FiuMD started as a fork of TorchMD and reworks its system representation, force evaluation, and integration to handle such heterogeneous batches. We test it with coarse-grained C$α$ models of chignolin, Trp-cage, BBL, and…

items.title: FMint-SDE: A Multimodal Foundation Model for Accelerating Numerical Simulation of SDEs via Error Correction
items.summary: Abstract. Fast and accurate simulation of dynamical systems is a fundamental challenge across scientific and engineering domains. Traditional numerical integrators often face a trade-off between accuracy and computational efficiency, while existing neural network–based approaches typically require training a separate model for each case. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a novel multimodal foundation model for large-scale simulations of differential equations: FMint-SDE (Foundation Model based on Initialization for stochastic differential equations). Based on a decoder-only transformer with in-context learning, FMint-SDE leverages numerical and textual modalities to learn a…

items.summary: Recursive self-improvement is a very promising aspect that can theoretically lead to a rapid intelligence explosion, where AI systems have the capability to radically improve themselves. This chapter will cover the foundations theoretically, the current state of the industry in this regard, the pathways that could be followed, the implications, and the potential of this recursive self-improvement of artificial intelligence systems being able to improve themselves. items.title: Symbiont
items.summary: Symbiont is a practical implementation of the ideas presented in "The Theory of Guided Symbiosis: A New Paradigm for Human Evolution in the Age of Superintelligence". That work views human nonlinearity and diversity as Useful Chaos: a living source of new hypotheses, adaptability, and unexpected directions of development, serving within GST as a resource for the long-term renewal of an intelligent system. Building on the mathematical foundation of GST Core V2, Symbiont translates this principle into a working architecture for human–model interaction. items.title: SEA-Lab: Experiment-grounded recursive self-improvement in an automated laboratory
items.summary: AI scientists can generate hypotheses, plans, and protocols. Translating these outputs into reliable experiments requires adapting them to local equipment and resources using feedback from observed outcomes. A key challenge is to retain laboratory execution feedback as reusable knowledge for subsequent planning. We present SEA-Lab (Self-Evolving Autonomous Lab), which combines an environment-grounded Dry-Lab Harness that generates protocols and machine-readable procedures, a wet-lab execution harness that coordinates heterogeneous devices and records execution traces and experimental measurements, and a recursive self-improvement mechanism that uses physical feedback to revise reusable…

items.title: From Verified Entanglement to Enforceable AI Safety: Assurance Conditions, Counterexamples, and a Bounded Authorization Protocol
items.summary: Can a genuine quantum signal authorize an unsafe action? A quantum signal may be genuine while the AI-controlled operation beside it violates a policy. This technical working paper examines what must connect physical verification to enforceable behavior. It combines a source-specific audit of IMCA+, an initialization-dependent quantum-circuit check, an observation-based counterexample, and a bounded authorization protocol with authenticated request binding, current policy epochs, protected replay state, evidence expiry, and complete mediation. items.title: NeuroMASS v4: Geometry-Aware Neural Population Dynamics via Learnable Hyperbolic Latent Representations and Biologically-Calibrated Diagonal State Space Models
items.summary: The geometry of neural population activity is a fundamental challenge in computational neuroscience. We present NeuroMASS v4, a novel architecture that introduces learnable hyperbolic latent geometry to spike-train co-smoothing on the Neural Latents Benchmark (NLB'21). Our central scientific claim is that the curvature c of a Poincaré-ball—learned end-to-end from extracellular spike recordings—constitutes a biologically interpretable geometric signature: significantly positive for ring-manifold motor circuits (MC_Maze, MC_RTT) and near-zero for topologically unstructured frontal circuits (DMFC_RSG). The architecture unifies five principled components: (i) discrete spike-count embed- dings…

items.title: Synergistic delivery of FSTL1 and CHIR99021 in 3D bioprinted patches promotes adult mammalian heart repair
items.summary: Recent advances in tissue engineering have positioned cardiac patch devices as a promising strategy to restore heart function and structure following myocardial infarction (MI). However, many existing patches are limited by the absence of vascular networks and insufficient biomolecular signals to effectively promote cardiomyocyte (CM) regeneration. In this study, we address these limitations by incorporating follistatin-like 1 (FSTL1) and CHIR99021 (CHIR) into a 3D bioprinted vascularized cardiac patch. The pro-proliferative effects of FSTL1 and CHIR on human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived CMs were validated in vitro using 2D cultures, 3D hydrogel casts, and 3D bioprinted…

items.title: Arithmetic-Geometric Foundations of Particle Generations: Modular Forms, Clifford Braids, and Hypercomplex Division Algebras
items.summary: The modularity theorem establishes a correspondence between elliptic curves and weight-2 modular forms , equating their -functions. The Clifford Braiding Theorem demonstrates that Clifford algebras admit unitary representations of the circular Artin braid group via operators constructed from anti-commuting generators. items.summary: Smooth continuum derivatives (Δx → 0, Δt → 0) and idempotent set operations ({a, a} = {a}) are mathematical idealizations that obscure discrete cycle counting and state conservation at the scale of individual Planck action quanta h. This paper formulates a coordinate-free discrete wave kinematics uniting Hilbert–Dirac state grammar with the real Euclidean Clifford algebra Cl(2,0) on the Punctured Euler–Clifford Plane (ECP). States are indexed by whole-cycle spatial density σ = n/Δx = p/h and event-locked temporal rate r = n/Δt = E/h, evolving along continuous (C⁰) polygonal chains of finite directed secant chords around a topologically excluded central void. items.summary: These research notes formulate a multivectorial and differential framework within the four-dimensional complexified Euclidean Clifford algebra Cl4(C) to construct four-vector potentials and field operators from the four-dimensional momentum stored in an interaction field. Using a local orthonormal tetrad with an imaginary tangential time axis, the relativistic energy-momentum component of a particle is expressed via the Clifford scalar product between its four-momentum and the temporal basis vector. Responsible AI describes the design, development, deployment, and use of AI systems ethically, fairly, transparently, and accountably, ensuring societal benefit while mitigating risks, errors, and patient harm. These elements are critical to protecting patient safety and preserving trust in this technology. Orthopaedic surgeons should recognize AI's potential to improve musculoskeletal care quality, efficiency, and outcomes while upholding these fundamentals. Endorsing these tenets commits our field to advancing AI aligned with the highest ethical, clinical, and operational…

items.title: Improving robustness of foundation model classification of rhabdoid features in clear cell renal cell carcinoma through mimicker-aware training.
An apicomplexan-specific foundation model improves prediction of regulatory genomic signals in Plasmodium falciparum
items.summary: Genomic foundation models learn transferable sequence representations through self-supervision, yet their practical value is contested. In data-rich mammalian genomes, task-specific models trained from scratch can match or exceed pretrained models on many regulatory prediction tasks. Whether self-supervised pretraining provides an advantage in small, data-sparse genomes has not been directly tested. We address this in the compact, 23Mbp, A/T-rich genome of the malaria parasite, Plasmodium falciparum. We trained a Genomic Pretrained Network (GPN) via masked-nucleotide reconstruction on 455 genome assemblies spanning 76 apicomplexan species. We then fine-tuned the model to predict a variety…

items.title: B-RANKO: An ncRNA Foundation Model with Bidirectional Decoder-Only Architecture
items.summary: Ribonucleic acid (RNA) plays central roles in gene expression, regulation and catalysis, and has emerged as an important target for therapeutic design. While recent RNA foundation models have achieved strong performance on representation learning tasks, relatively few approaches support both native sequence generation and transferable representation learning within a single framework. We present B-RANKO, a 150M-parameter bidirectional decoder-only ncRNA foundation model that introduces a novel bidirectional autoregressive attention mechanism, enabling a single architecture to support both de novo sequence generation and representation learning. Pretrained on a large corpus derived from…

items.title: Learning gene co-regulation across cells with Multicellular Transformer
items.summary: Understanding how genes coordinate across cells is central to explaining tissue function and disease, yet most existing models still take a single cell as input and therefore emphasize cell-intrinsic regulation. We present the Multicellular Transformer (MCT), a foundation model built around a different assumption: cells function together within tissues, so the appropriate unit of input is not one cell in isolation but a set of cells from the same sample. By jointly modeling multiple cells, MCT learns context-aware gene embeddings that capture gene-gene interactions across the tissue environment. Trained on a large set of tissue samples (>4200) across more than 30 tissue types, MCT recovers…

items.title: Feasibility of chronic kidney disease classification using bilateral kidney ultrasound and foundation model representations
items.summary: Abstract Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a major global health burden, yet early diagnosis remains challenging and conventional kidney ultrasonography is limited by operator dependence and low sensitivity to subtle textural changes. We investigated the feasibility of an ultrasound foundation model for CKD classification from bilateral kidney ultrasound images, with reference labels defined using an operational subset of the Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) 2024 guidelines. In this retrospective single-center study, 13,245 kidney ultrasound images from 1,484 patients (1,128 with CKD and 356 without) were analyzed. The Universal Ultrasound Foundation Model (USFM) was…

items.title: Quantifying multi-lesion detection and localization in whole-body FDG PET/CT with a multimodal foundation model.
items.summary: Objective . To develop a three-dimensional AI framework for detecting and localizing multiple lesions in whole-body FDG PET/CT, and to evaluate whether a pretrained PET/CT multimodal foundation model can improve lesion detection performance compared with conventional training from scratch. Approach . The AutoPET cohort comprised 1014 studies divided into 700 training, 114 validation, and 200 subject-independent test studies. Lesion masks were converted into three-dimensional bounding boxes. We developed a one-stage 3D lesion detector using a PlainConvUNet backbone to extract multi-scale encoder-decoder features for lesion classification and box regression. To leverage foundation-model…

items.title: Condensates increase the frequency of transcription.
items.summary: While biomolecular condensates have been implicated in activating transcription, investigating the specific contributions of condensates relative to soluble proteins has been challenging. Here, we leverage the concentration dependence of condensate formation to compare the transcriptional activity of condensed and soluble MYOCD, a cell-type-specific transcriptional coactivator. Using single-cell resolution measurements, we find that cells with MYOCD condensates have more target gene transcripts than cells with soluble MYOCD. While transcription can occur in the absence of condensates, it is less frequent and produces fewer transcripts. Both the frequency of active cells and transcriptional…

items.title: A Plasma eMTBR-Tau Immunoassay for Detection of Advanced Insoluble Tau Pathology.
items.summary: Blood biomarkers that reflect neurofibrillary tau burden, a defining hallmark of Alzheimer disease (AD), remain limited. Endogenously cleaved microtubule-binding region tau 243 (eMTBR-tau243) has shown promise when measured by mass spectrometry; a scalable immunoassay could broaden research access and support clinical evaluation. To determine whether plasma levels of eMTBR-tau measured by a novel immunoassay are associated with tau neurofibrillary tangle pathology defined by neuropathology and tau positron emission tomography (PET). This cross-sectional study included brain donors with antemortem plasma from 2 US autopsy cohorts, and individuals with plasma samples and tau PET from 2…

items.title: Full-length β-tubulin sequencing of Trichuris trichiura in South Korea reveals novel variants with a conserved benzimidazole-binding pocket.
items.summary: Trichuris trichiura remains difficult to control with benzimidazoles, and the genetic mechanisms underlying treatment response in human populations remain poorly understood. Canonical β-tubulin mutations (F167Y, E198A, F200Y) drive benzimidazole resistance in veterinary nematodes, but their prevalence, distribution, and functional impact in human whipworms are largely uncharacterized. South Korea's current low-transmission status creates an ideal setting to examine present-day parasite lineages after decades of sustained deworming. We analyzed 18 T. trichiura isolates collected between 2017 and 2025 using long-read sequencing of the full β-tubulin locus and the ITS2 region, combined with…

items.title: Centrosome identity drives asymmetric microtubule-dependent pushing forces, spindle positioning and daughter cell size
items.summary: Mitotic spindle positioning is essential for tissue architecture and organogenesis. In Drosophila neural stem cells, spindle positioning is attributed to apically enriched Dynein generating pulling forces on astral microtubules (MTs). Surprisingly, however, we find that the mitotic spindle consistently adopts a basal position along the apico-basal polarity axis, challenging the canonical model. We show that centrosomes at opposite spindle poles retain an intrinsic asymmetry in MT nucleation capacity inherited from their mother-daughter identity, with the apical daughter centrosome nucleating more MTs than the basal mother centrosome. Equalizing or reversing this asymmetry alters spindle…

items.title: Dog shelter facilitated transmission and maintenance of benzimidazole resistance-associated alleles in canine hookworms
items.summary: Anthelmintic resistance in canine hookworms is increasingly recognised; however, environmental settings that maintain and disseminate resistance-associated alleles remain poorly defined. We hypothesised that urban dog shelters act as hotspots for transmission of benzimidazole resistance-associated alleles in Ancylostoma caninum. Residual faecal samples (n=173) were collected from a Sydney, Australia metropolitan shelter over four sampling periods and analysed using coprodiagnostic methods and deep amplicon sequencing targeting ITS-2 and isotype-1 β-tubulin loci. Hookworm eggs were detected in 41% of samples, with A. caninum identified in 97% of sequenced infections and U. stenocephala in…

items.title: Spindle minus-end microtubule protrusions perturb force balance and delay chromosome segregation
items.summary: Mitotic spindle function depends on multiple forces that are difficult to measure in cells. In fission yeast, the spindle assembles and elongates within an intact nuclear envelope. Without the kinesin-14/Pkl1, spindle microtubule minus ends detach from the spindle pole body and are pushed beyond it by kinesin-5/Cut7 sliding, forming protrusions that deform the nuclear envelope. We quantified and modeled protrusion dynamics. We found that as protrusions grew, the spindle often shortened, and the extent of shortening correlated with loss of spindle Cut7. Cells with protrusions showed a delay in anaphase onset. A force-balance model can explain fast and slow protrusion length changes, and…

items.title: Morphology and phylogenomics of Leucomyxa quisqueyensis sp. nov., a colorless freshwater amoeboid ochrophyte (Stramenopiles) from the Dominican Republic
items.summary: Amoeboid ochrophytes (stramenopiles) exhibit diverse cell forms and plastid states, yet many lineages are known primarily from environmental sequences. We describe Leucomyxa quisqueyensis sp. nov., a freshwater amoeboid ochrophyte isolated from a freshwater drainage channel in La Chinola, Santo Domingo Oeste, Dominican Republic. In established cultures, the isolate consistently formed extensive multinucleate reticula, with fine strands linking densely branched regions. The largest networks exceeded 2 mm. Confocal imaging revealed longitudinal microtubule strands along the reticulopodia. Rounded cysts measured 6.47-15.43 um in diameter. SSU rRNA and nuclear phylogenomic analyses identified…

items.title: N-terminal mutations R5L and R5H share a common mechanism in disrupting tau condensates on microtubule surfaces
items.summary: Tau, an intrinsically disordered protein abundant in neuronal axons, forms cooperative condensates on microtubule (MT) surfaces that regulate motor proteins and protect MTs from severing enzymes. Disease-associated mutations at residue 5 in the N-terminal projection domain of tau, far from the MT-tau binding interface, have been linked to progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) (R5L) and frontotemporal dementia (FTD) (R5H). While R5L was previously shown to disrupt tau condensate formation on MT surfaces, it remained unclear whether R5H shares this phenotype. Using total internal reflection fluorescence (TIRF) microscopy, we show that both mutations reduce condensate packing density compared…

items.title: Voltage-Driven Transition from Steady-State Fluctuations to Phase-Transition Noise in Nanoscale VO2 Devices.
items.summary: We investigate the electrically driven metal-to-insulator transition (MIT) in a nanoscale vanadium dioxide (VO2) Mott memristor through noise spectroscopy and two-dimensional resistor network simulations. Our experiments focus on both the insulating phase as the applied voltage approaches the threshold voltage (set transition) and the metallic phase as the voltage is reduced toward the reset voltage (reset transition). In both regimes, we observe an order-of-magnitude increase in relative current noise near the transition points. To analyze the origin of this noise enhancement, we use simulations that capture the stochastic dynamics of the phase transition. The simulations indicate that…

items.title: Stimulus-Driven Reconfigurable Memristors with Volatile-to-Nonvolatile Transition for Spatiotemporal Neuromorphic Computing.
items.summary: Neuromorphic hardware for spatiotemporal information processing requires both transient dynamics and programmable weight storage, whereas existing implementations typically rely either on heterogeneous integration of volatile dynamic units and nonvolatile memory devices or on compliance-current regulation to reconfigure volatile/nonvolatile operation within a single device, increasing device diversity or peripheral control complexity. This work reports a stimulus-reconfigurable Ag/ZnS/FTO memristor in which the stability of Ag conductive pathways is regulated by the strength and temporal scale of external stimuli, enabling volatile short-term dynamics and nonvolatile conductance modulation…

items.title: Multicolor coupling perception enabled by a C8-BTBT/MoS 2 p-n junction phototransistor.
items.summary: Mimicking biological multicolor perception remains a key challenge for artificial vision systems. Herein, we developed a C8-BTBT/MoS 2 p-n junction phototransistor that mimics retinal trichromatic coupling through spatiotemporal dynamics and neuromorphic plasticity. The photogenerated carriers separate through the photovoltaic effect between p-type C8-BTBT and n-type MoS 2 , enhancing the photoresponse and inducing photogating-mediated memory. Following the Bienenstock-Cooper-Munro (BCM) learning rule, the device exhibited wavelength-selective synaptic plasticity. Short-wavelength light (450 nm) triggered rapid carrier dynamics and strong memory, whereas long-wavelength light (635 nm)…

items.title: Solution-processed polyimide memristors for high-performance and reconfigurable T-type radio-frequency routing.
items.summary: Radio-frequency (RF) switches are essential for reconfigurable wireless front-ends that require low-loss transmission, high isolation, and ideally zero-static-power operation. Memristive RF switches are promising because their programmed low-resistance state (LRS) and high-resistance state (HRS) can respectively provide low-loss RF ON transmission and low-parasitic RF OFF isolation. For flexible and integrated front-ends, polymer memristive switches are attractive because solution-processable and mechanically compliant dielectric layers can be formed over large areas. However, the connection between polymer transport physics, RF parasitics, mechanical compliance, and circuit-level routing…

items.title: Weights & Caches: LLMs Can Program Tabular Foundation Models
items.summary: Neural networks are typically programmed through optimization, rather than by explicitly specifying their computations. Recent work on weight-space programming suggests that large language models (LLMs) can instead reason about and manipulate neural-network weights directly. In this work, we show that LLMs can directly program statistical computations in tabular foundation models (TFMs), whose parameters enable inference across different datasets. We investigate three complementary settings using GPT-6 Astra, without gradient-based optimization. First, Astra directly programs nanoTabPFN from zero-initialized weights, achieving a mean ROC AUC of 0.849 across 20 TabArena datasets, compared…

items.title: Symmetry Fingerprinting with Geometric Learnable Invariants Transformers
items.summary: Geometric deep learning has made available a large variety of structurally equivariant neural network architectures, meaning a particular transformation of their input causes a predictable transformation of their output. But structural equivariance is a very strong inductive bias that can limit performance if chosen poorly. In contrast, choosing an architecture with low geometric bias necessitates data augmentation to obtain correct behavior; extending the training process. We propose a novel neural network architecture that is soft equivariant; we select a set of symmetry groups and during training the network will become equivariant only to those symmetry groups that are appropriate…

items.title: Submatrices of character tables and centers of ordinary and queer q-Schur superalgebras
items.summary: We obtain bases of the centers of the ordinary $q$-Schur superalgebra $\mathcal{S}_q(m|n,r)$ and the queer $q$-Schur superalgebra $\mathcal{Q}_q(n,r)$ in terms of Casimir elements of the Hecke algebra $\mathcal{H}_r$ and the Hecke-Clifford algebra $\mathcal{H}_r^c$, respectively. items.title: MoViC: Real-Time Humanoid Whole-Body Control from Monocular Video Streams
items.summary: Real-time whole-body imitation from monocular video requires both a robust universal tracker and high-quality real-time reconstruction. We present MoViC, a framework that uses live RGB video as a control signal for humanoid robots without wearable tracking devices. The framework combines monocular human motion reconstruction, robot retargeting, and a transformer-based behavior foundation model. The policy receives proprioceptive history, a single explicit next-step reference, and a compact frequency-domain motion representation that supplies temporal context without explicitly stacking future reference frames, which reduces the input dimension and network size. During deployment, our…

items.title: Is the Bitter Lesson coming to genomic prediction? An untuned tabular foundation model matches or beats specialized methods
items.summary: Genomic prediction (GP) is dominated by models designed around assumptions about how genetic variation affects phenotypes. Here we asked how well a general-purpose pretrained tabular foundation model called TabPFN-3.5 does with no genetics-specific modeling and no tuning when given marker genotypes directly. We benchmarked TabPFN-3.5 using a published comparison of 18 GP methods on 18 traits in six plant species. Against the published means, TabPFN-3.5 ranked first on 11 of 18 traits and had the best median rank. Because the published benchmark did not identify its test sets, we reran GBLUP, RKHS and elastic-net models on the same splits as TabPFN-3.5. Against the best of these, TabPFN-3.5…

items.title: Tailoring Ion Exchange Efficiency in Synaptic Electrochemical Memtransistors Through Three-Dimensional Artificial Crystal Engineering.
items.summary: Electronic synapses featuring conduction modulation for synaptic weight update play a central role in implementing neuromorphic computing. Though memristors and memtransistors operating via ion exchange for conductance modulation have demonstrated synaptic functionality, their planar architectures suffer from a reduced interfacial area during lateral scaling, limiting their dynamic range of conductance modulation. Here, an electrochemical memtransistor is presented that replaces conventional planar layout with a precisely engineered 3D structure composed of an SU-8 organic reservoir and ZnO channel, fabricated using proximity-field nanopatterning. This design increases the effective oxygen…

items.title: From Quantum Brain to Quantum Mind: The Ontological Promotion Gap in Quantum-Biological Theories of Consciousness.
items.summary: Quantum effects in biological systems are increasingly investigated at molecular, cellular, and neural scales, yet evidence for quantum organization in a living brain does not by itself determine the ontological status of the conscious states realized by that brain. This article distinguishes seven claims often compressed under "quantum consciousness": quantum occurrence, causal relevance, constitutive relevance, phenomenal bridging, phenomenal individuation, quantum mental status, and quantum-formal adequacy. It argues that evidence for the first three-even if decisive-does not by itself establish quantum mental status. I call this cross-level inferential discontinuity the Ontological…

items.title: BioLM-Score: Language-Prior Conditioned Probabilistic Geometric Potentials for Protein-Ligand Scoring.
items.summary: Motivation Protein-ligand scoring must address affinity prediction, pose selection, and virtual screening, but these objectives are not necessarily optimized together. Geometric likelihood models may generalize poorly when training-set structural coverage is limited. We test whether pretrained biomolecular representations improve scoring under a controlled geometric baseline. Results BioLM-Score integrates frozen protein and molecular language-model embeddings into a residue-atom distance-likelihood framework via gated graph convolutions. We evaluate geometry-only, jointly trained, and two-stage fine-tuned variants, using the jointly trained variant for the primary controlled comparisons.…

items.title: GenAI-enabled accounting information systems competence: Antecedents, perceived usefulness, AI ethics awareness, and career readiness outcomes.
items.summary: This study examines GenAI-enabled accounting information systems competence (GAISC) among accounting and auditing students and its relationships with GenAI readiness (GAR), perceived ease of use (PEOU), digital learning self-efficacy (DLSE), facilitating conditions (FC), perceived usefulness (PU), AI ethics awareness (AIEA), and career readiness (CR). The model is anchored in Socio-Technical Systems Theory (STS) and Social Cognitive Career Theory (SCCT), with technology readiness, TAM, self-efficacy, and facilitating-condition logic used as construct-level underpinning mechanisms. Survey data from 471 students at five Vietnamese universities were analyzed using PLS-SEM, complemented by a…

items.title: Candidate alternative splice-junction architecture at a Ganoderma carnitine acetyltransferase-like locus: an accession-traceable RNA-seq reanalysis
items.summary: Abstract A focused reanalysis of public Ganoderma transcriptomic resources evaluated two candidate splice-junction paths (A and B) at a putative carnitine acetyltransferase-like locus (MSTRG.5584). Forty RNA-seq run labels from five genomic backgrounds were reconciled with accession metadata and examined using targeted splice-spanning read counts; 11 undercovered libraries underwent complete read-1 recounting. Both candidate junction paths were observed in all five backgrounds. In libraries with any focal read support, mean junction-A fractions were descriptively greater in mycelium-labeled than in fruiting-body-labeled groups, with background-level differences ranging from +0.190 to…

items.summary: Degenerate horizons of black holes surrounded by a Kiselev quintessence fluid open into two product throats: a Nariai region dS2 × S2$ when the black-hole and cosmological horizons merge, and a Bertotti–Robinson region AdS2 × S2 when the charged hole becomes extremal. items.title: Effect of xanthan gum on 3D-printed dysphagia foods.
items.summary: Background The global trend of population ageing is progressively worsening, leading to an increasing prevalence of dysphagia among the elderly population. Meanwhile, 3D printing technology offers a viable solution by providing customized, nutrient-rich, dysphagia-friendly foods for affected individuals. This study utilized Pleurotus ostreatus mycelium (POM), xanthan gum (XG), and egg white protein as primary materials. items.summary: Developing high-dimensional solid-state quantum technologies requires overcoming the trade-off between spin dimensionality and quantum coherence. Hybrid spin architectures offer a promising solution to expand the quantum state space bottom-up by combining rapid electronic manipulation with robust nuclear phase memory. items.summary: CRISPR-based lineage recording technologies can trace the ancestry of hundreds of thousands of cells, yet reconstructing accurate phylogenies at this scale remains computationally challenging. Likelihood-based methods employ explicit evolutionary models of CRISPR editing that improve tree accuracy but require computationally expensive searches over tree topologies, whereas greedy distance-based alternatives scale efficiently but their accuracy requires distances that faithfully represent the true phylogeny. items.title: Where the Loop Meets the Budget: Analyzing On-Device Recursive Self-Improvement
items.summary: Persistent self-improvement enables language-model agents to adapt from experience, but its update process competes with inference for limited device memory, energy, and thermal headroom. Existing surveys largely examine self-improvement mechanisms and on-device learning separately, providing limited guidance on how update reliability and device costs should be assessed together. We introduce a unified taxonomy that organizes persistent updates by component, execution locus, feedback, loop closure, timescale, and budget, and distinguishes recursive changes to evaluators or update machinery. items.title: How many labels can a biological oscillator carry? A quality-factor screen for proposed information carriers.
items.summary: How many distinguishable labels can a biological oscillator carry? Proposals invoking collective vibrational modes, endogenous electromagnetic fields, microtubule excitations and oscillatory phase codes are each debated on grounds particular to themselves, with no shared standard for comparison. items.title: Integration and annotation of spatial multi-omic data with DIRAC.
items.summary: Spatial multi-omic technologies measure multiple molecular layers within intact tissues. Two central challenges are vertical integration, which combines different molecular modalities, and horizontal integration, which aligns cell types across studies. Here we show domain invariant representation through adaptive calibration (DIRAC), a geometric deep learning model that unifies these tasks in a generalized domain adaptation framework. items.title: When, Where, and How Experience Becomes Structure: Mechanisms for Recursive Self-Improvement in LLM Agents
items.summary: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) studies how AI systems modify themselves and carry those changes into the generation of subsequent improvements. LLM agents can pursue this process by using interaction experience to revise Prompt, Memory, Skill, and Harness in some cases while keeping the task-execution model’s weights fixed. However, execution feedback does not directly specify which component should change, and a locally successful revision may not remain useful across tasks or subsequent improvement cycles. items.title: Hierarchical semantic fusion in hyperbolic space for next POI recommendation.
items.summary: Next Point-of-Interest (POI) recommendation aims to suggest POIs that users are likely to visit next based on their recent check-ins. Recent studies suggest that POI-POI transitions and user-POI interactions exhibit hierarchical patterns that can be modeled in hyperbolic space, whose exponential volume growth enables compact and expressive representations. items.title: Learning inhibitor interactions from protein deep mutational scanning data and deep learning models
items.summary: Recent advances in protein language models, geometric deep learning, and structure prediction frameworks have the potential to accelerate computational drug discovery. However, it remains unclear how well these methods generalize beyond their training sets. Mutation-dependent drug responses present a challenge to these methods because there are often large effects from relatively small perturbations. items.summary: Open-vocabulary 3D scene graph generation aims to predict 3D objects and their predicates beyond the annotated label space. Compared to closed-set 3D scene graph generation methods, the open-vocabulary approach is more general, practical, and less dependent on labor-intensive ground truth annotations. items.summary: Understanding how protein environments regulate the photodynamics of chromophores is a central task in quantum biology and remains a major challenge. items.title: From Harness Optimization to Recursive Self-Improvement: A Survey of Language Model Agents
items.summary: Language-model agents rely on harnesses that govern tool use, context, memory, and execution. Understanding automated harness revision requires connecting improvement methods to the reusable functionality they produce. This survey examines three linked perspectives: improvement workflows, recursive scope, and concrete modifications across task domains. We compare search strategies, memory management, edit guidance, and integration with model training, and use an existing five-level framework to distinguish harness optimization from recursive self-improvement. items.title: AI4AI: Toward AI-Discovered Superintelligence
items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping how AI itself is developed. From designing learning algorithms to automating research workflows and evaluation, this expanding role has fueled the rapid growth of AI for AI (AI4AI).
